books.freeSourceNote: Internet Archive free borrow. How to calculate real markup that produces actual profit for trades and service businesses.

notes: Matches the founder's own honest finding, with more nuance: Nigeria has real, current, well-developed content here (Business Elites Africa, WithinNigeria, Writertain Creatives, Anutio) but it teaches freelancing logistics (which platforms pay in dollars, which payment rails avoid conversion loss) — not the further step of turning that income into a product or agency, which is what this category needs. Business Elites Africa's specific RSS feed could not be confirmed this round (a broader Nigeria-business RSS search surfaced many real adjacent blogs but not this exact one) — worth a direct, narrower search rather than guessing. On books: both candidates (The SaaS Playbook, Company of One) are commercially paid; the only 'free' copies found were on piracy sites (Yumpu, Scribd re-uploads) or were third-party paid summary services (Shortform, Four Minute Books) rather than the actual free book — neither counts, so left at 0 rather than substitute either.
actionRequired: 2026-08-04: Removed generic personal-dev books (Atomic Habits etc.) and pure-news blogs (BusinessDay, Nairametrics, Connect Nigeria, BellaNaija). Replaced with free practical business books (E-Myth, Profit First, Markup & Profit, How Much Should I Charge?, Lean Startup, Rework, Personal MBA, Traction, Company of One, OpenStax Entrepreneurship) and Nigerian/African SME blogs. Priority: Nigeria → Africa → Global. All books free.

2026-08-04 full audit: Removed pure-technical tutorials, pure-news and generic personal-dev sources. Kept/replaced with category-specific business operations content (pricing, clients, cash flow, systems, scaling). Books forced free (IA/OpenStax/Bookdio/author free). Priority Nigeria→Africa→Global.
